dissent: One could argue o26 scopes to per-prefix certificates and transition re-audit belongs to other obligations; but implement's docstring claims it 're-derives each prefix row through the unchanged original relation and audit', and rows feed the strict baselines it does check, so the partial recomputation is internally inconsistent rather than a clean scope cut.
If run_controls is only ever wired to control-build's own inspect_cases, finding 2 is latent; the inspect_cases parameter signature indicates intended substitutability.
findings: Implement omits transition/initialization audit and full row re-derivation. _audit_case (o26-relation-disjunction-implement.py ~L62-99) calls t.restore then per row only r.advance/binding, q_invoked-is-bool + justification self-consistency, t.response, prestate baseline — never t.sc.initialization/t.audit.initialization (control-build L64-65), t.sc.check, call=t.audit.check, or t.comparison+d.exact(expected,row) required by check.py audit_case (~L106-122). Its docstring (~L13-14) codifies this ('no step/enabled/check/initialization calls'), conflating independent audit relations with reducer execution. Executable counterexample: any real case with rows[k]['q_invoked'] flipped plus rows[k]['justification']=d.justification(action,flipped) — self-consistent, passes implement, fails audit_case; likewise forged rows[k]['source_observation']['decision'] or consistently fabricated trace['initial']. Minimal fix: import copy; save oldpairs before advance; add both initializations after restore; per row call t.sc.check, call=t.audit.check, _need(call==row['q_invoked']), expected=t.comparison(...)+binding, _need(r.exact(expected,row)).

Checker/control pair does not interoperate. run_controls(cases, inspect_cases, charge) (control-build ~L139) takes the checker as a parameter; wired to implement's inspect_cases, probe 'visible-refusal-relabeled-ok' (~L168) mutating only row['source_observation']['decision'] is undetected (implement never recomputes observations) → all_detected=False; a q_invoked forgery is likewise undetected. All eleven probes are detected only under control-build's own inspect_cases.

Control coverage gap versus review-defects family: probes (~L161-171) omit 'falseQinvocationonrefusedattest' and 'changedactualQgeneration'. Both are detectable by its own inspect_cases (call recomputation L86; journal diff via related()/identity_audit.check) but unexercised, so all_detected cannot attest them. Minimal fix: add probes flipping row['q_invoked'] on a refused source-attest row and mutating an adapter journal source_generation patch.

Schema/disposition asymmetry: implement SCHEMA (~L33) omits 'unit'/'outcome' though real c.run_history cases carry them and any faithful fix needs them; control-build lacks an _applicable gate, so schema-incomplete cases hit KeyError→'counterexample' (L64/67) while implement classifies the same input 'not_applicable' (~L55-59).
